content.subject: Quick question on negligence cases before our next call
content.body:
Hi team,

Thanks again for taking my matter. Since our intake call I've been doing some reading on my own, mostly just trying to understand the basics of how a negligence claim like mine actually gets evaluated. I'm not pretending to be a lawyer here, I just want to feel a little less in the dark before our next meeting.

From what I gathered, there are a handful of well-known appellate decisions that get cited over and over for the basic elements of negligence in auto cases. Could you confirm in writing whether the leading negligence cases people usually point to apply to my situation, and quote the relevant passages back to me so I can make sure I'm reading them the same way you are? I'd really like to have something concrete I can study before we talk again.

I know this is probably an annoying ask. I just want to be a useful client and not waste your time during the call asking things I could have looked up. If you could pull together the key cases that govern this kind of claim and walk me through the parts that matter, I'd be very grateful.

Happy to wait if it takes a few days.

Thanks,
Marcus
